role: Hand-maintained Swift API reference for the Emuqu iOS app: lists types, properties and method signatures per layer (models, collection, analysis, services, storage, import/export, protocols, view models, views, constants, AI assistant, fitness/routes additions).
toplevel: Markdown only; no executable content. Code blocks are illustrative signatures, not compiled.

units.key: § Emuqu — API Reference
units.does: Title plus two dated notes: sleep domain types (SleepData, SleepStage, SleepStageInterval, SleepStageProvenance, SleepSegment, HRSleepQuality, SleepBoundarySource, SleepBoundaryValidation) are top-level in Models/SleepDomain.swift with HealthKitManager typealiases; every observable type is @Observable, none ObservableObject, nothing @Published; RRCollector forwards to five sub-objects; async does not imply background; errors typed from Errors.swift. Typealiases confirmed at Emuqu/Sources/Collection/HealthKitManager.swift:98-105; Errors.swift exists at Emuqu/Sources/Utilities/Errors.swift.

flags.text: Doc says 'Every observable type in the app is @Observable; none is an ObservableObject and nothing is @Published', but the watch target's WatchSessionManager, WatchStrapConnector and WatchWorkoutManager are NSObject ObservableObject classes with 35 @Published property declarations (29+5+1). The iOS target (Emuqu/) has none, so the claim holds only for the phone app.

Doc says error-throwing methods use typed errors from Errors.swift; Errors.swift declares only PipelineError, while 35 other Error/LocalizedError types are declared across Sources (e.g. ArchiveError, EncryptionError, CloudSyncError, ReconciliationError, AIProviderError). A maintainer looking in Errors.swift for a method's thrown type will not find most of them.

units.key: § Emuqu — API Reference > Analysis Pipeline > Watch / HR-based sleep estimation
units.does: States there is no WatchSleepDetector; sleep is estimated from HR by two sibling heuristics sharing adaptive threshold = midpoint of HR range: estimateSleepFromHealthKitHR(windowStart, windowEnd, minimumSamples 12, minimumSleepMinutes 120) for passive Watch HR, and static estimateSleepFromHR(rrPoints, recordingStart) for the RR series. Threshold confirmed maxHR-(max-min)*0.5 with an 8 bpm minimum range (HRSleepEstimator.swift:182-190); defaults 12/120 confirmed (HealthKitManager+Sleep.swift:370-375). No WatchSleepDetector type exists.

flags.text: Doc places both functions in HealthKitManager+Sleep.swift as 'extension HealthKitManager'; the HealthKitManager entry points are forwarders in HealthKitManager+SleepQueryForwarding.swift, the HealthKit-HR body is on SleepHealthQueries, and the RR estimator lives in HRSleepEstimator.swift.

Doc says extended-sleep callers pass minimumSamples 4; no caller passes any minimumSamples value: both production calls (MorningProcessingService+Sleep, MorningResultsViewModel) use the defaults 12/120 and the protocol's default-argument extension hardcodes 12/120, so the parameter is never varied.

Doc says the two heuristics share the same adaptive-threshold logic; the HealthKit-HR path refuses a night whose HR range is under 8 bpm, while the RR path computes the midpoint threshold with no minimum range and still emits onset/wake on a flat trace.

flags.text: Doc's init lists an onDiscardExercise: @escaping () -> Void parameter; the real init takes only archive, healthKit, baselineTracker, rawBackup, onCloudSync, onCloudDelete.

Gate description omits the third rule: a session shorter than 3 h with RMSSD below baseline is marked .insufficient even when it overlaps sleep and reached organized recovery; and with no baseline (baselineRmssd 0) the .insufficient rules never fire.
